answer_1.quote: Legal fact prediction (LFP) aims to take the evidence submitted by litigants for trial as input and automatically determine relevant legal facts... the LFP task requires a system f that takes the tuple (C, Z) as input and yields a set of legal facts f(C, Z).
answer_1.outputs: predicted legal facts (textual descriptions) used for downstream judgment prediction

answer_2.quote: we employ three metrics: (1) ROUGE ; (2) ChatLaw-based similarity, which calculates the distance between the predicted and ground-truth facts based on their embeddings determined by the ChatLaw-Text2Vecw model ; and (3) LLM-Judge scores assigned by GPT-4o on a ten-point scale.

answer_3.quote: LLM-Judge scores assigned by GPT-4o on a ten-point scale.

answer_4.quote: we asked our two legal experts to perform evidence-based LJP using our dataset, i.e., to predict the judgment outcomes solely based on the extracted evidence. They were required to evaluate a randomly selected sample of 100 cases, comprising a total of 259 plaintiff claims.
answer_4.guideline: Legal experts assessed the correctness of the predicted judgments, reporting overall accuracy.
